item.title: Global tech stocks slide as AI disruption fears spread
item.description:
Asian equities retreated from record highs on Friday as a fresh wave of concern over artificial intelligence's disruptive potential swept through global markets, triggering sharp losses in technology stocks from Tokyo to Mumbai.

The selloff began on Wall Street Thursday, where the S&P 500 fell 1.6% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2% as investors fled software and tech shares perceived as vulnerable to AI-driven automation, according to Bloomberg. The rout spread to Asia on Friday, with Japan's Nikkei 225 falling 1.2%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index declining 1.7%, and the Shanghai Composite shedding 1.3%.

item.title: UN approves global AI scientific panel despite US objections
item.description:
The United Nations General Assembly voted overwhelmingly Thursday to establish a 40-member global scientific panel dedicated to assessing the impacts and risks of artificial intelligence, overriding strong objections from the United States.

The vote in the 193-member assembly was 117-2, with the United States and Paraguay voting against the measure, while Tunisia and Ukraine abstained. American allies in Europe, Asia, and elsewhere voted in favor alongside Russia, China, and many developing nations, marking a rare instance of broad international consensus on technology governance that excluded Washington.

item.title: Helion hits 150 million degrees in private fusion first
item.description:
Helion Energy announced Friday that its Polaris prototype reactor has reached plasma temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius and demonstrated measurable deuterium-tritium fusion, becoming the first privately developed fusion machine to achieve both milestones. The breakthroughs represent major steps toward the company's goal of delivering commercial fusion power to Microsoft by 2028.

The Washington-based startup began operating its seventh-generation Polaris prototype at the end of 2024 and in January became the first private fusion company to use deuterium-tritium fuel after obtaining regulatory approval to possess and use tritium for fusion energy demonstration.

item.title: Spain, Poland see inflation fall to multi-month lows in January
item.description: Fresh inflation data released Friday showed price pressures continuing to ease in both Spain and Poland, while India rolled out a revamped consumer price index designed to better capture modern spending patterns.

item.title: DP World replaces CEO and chairman after Epstein file fallout
item.description:
Dubai-based ports giant DP World announced major leadership changes on Friday, naming Essa Kazim as chairman and Yuvraj Narayan as group chief executive officer, replacing Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem who had held both positions for decades. The reshuffling comes amid mounting pressure on the company following the release of U.S. Justice Department files linking bin Sulayem to Jeffrey Epstein, the disgraced financier and convicted sex offender who died in 2019.

The announcement, made by Dubai Media Office, follows suspensions of new investments by the UK's British International Investment and Canada's La Caisse pension fund over the Epstein revelations.

item.title: Rubio arrives in Munich, says he expects to meet Zelensky
item.description:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he expects to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at the 62nd Munich Security Conference, which began Friday amid heightened tensions over Russia's war in Ukraine and fraying transatlantic relations.

"I think he's going to be there and there's a chance to see him. I believe it's on my schedule, not 100% certain, but I'm sure we will," Rubio told CNN en route to Germany. The meeting is anticipated for Saturday, when Zelenskyy is expected to arrive at the conference.

The annual gathering at the Bayerischer Hof hotel has drawn more than 60 heads of state and government, alongside roughly 100 foreign and defense ministers, making it one of the largest in the forum's history. The Munich Security Conference confirmed on social media that Rubio is leading "the largest US delegation we have ever welcomed in Munich," which includes more than 50 members of Congress.

item.title: Ukraine tricks Russian troops with fake Starlink service
item.description:
Ukrainian cyber activists announced Thursday that they had successfully executed an elaborate sting operation against Russian forces desperate to restore Starlink satellite internet connectivity, collecting thousands of data points on enemy positions and terminal information while pocketing nearly $6,000 from Moscow's troops.

The 256th Cyber Assault Division, working alongside open-source intelligence groups InformNapalm and MILITANT, created a network of fake Telegram channels and bots that appeared to offer Russian soldiers help registering their Starlink terminals on a Ukrainian government whitelist, according to statements from the groups and confirmed by Ukraine's Defense Ministry.

item.title: Germany's Merz rebukes 'MAGA culture war' at Munich conference
item.description:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz opened the Munich Security Conference on Friday by acknowledging a deep divide between the United States and Europe while urging both sides to rebuild trust through a new partnership framework.

In his keynote address, Merz warned that the post-World War II international order "no longer exists in that form" and called on European nations to strengthen their defense capabilities while keeping the transatlantic alliance intact.

"A rift has opened up between Europe and the United States," Merz said, directly referencing Vice President JD Vance's confrontational speech at the same conference a year earlier. But he pushed back sharply against the cultural criticisms Vance leveled at European governments: "The culture war of the MAGA movement is not ours. Freedom of speech ends here with us when that speech goes against human dignity and the constitution."

item.title: Yangtze fish biomass more than doubled after five-year ban
item.description:
Fish biomass in China's Yangtze River has more than doubled and endangered species populations are recovering, according to new research documenting the effects of an unprecedented decade-long commercial fishing ban that began in 2021.

A peer-reviewed study published Thursday in the journal Science found that the full fishing ban has halted seven decades of biodiversity decline in Asia's longest river, with fish biomass increasing by a median of 209% and species richness rising by 13%. The findings arrive as China marks the halfway point of its ambitious conservation effort, which required resettling more than 231,000 fishers and recalling 111,000 fishing boats at a cost exceeding $2.74 billion.

item.title: Trump administration escalates pressure on Ukraine for peace deal
item.description:
The Trump administration is intensifying demands on Ukraine to accept territorial compromises and hold elections to end the war with Russia by early summer, according to Ukrainian officials cited by The New York Times on Friday.

The pressure comes as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio are set to meet at the Munich Security Conference, which begins February 13. Ukrainian officials reported that Washington is pushing harder on Kyiv than on Moscow to reach a settlement before the November US midterm elections, with negotiations potentially resuming as early as next week.

item.title: Musk's bankers work to refinance $18B debt ahead of SpaceX IPO
item.description:
Elon Musk's banking team is working on a potential financing strategy that could reduce the heavy interest burden the billionaire has accumulated through years of acquisitions, according to Bloomberg.

The refinancing effort comes less than two weeks after SpaceX officially completed its merger with xAI on February 2, creating the world's most valuable private company with a combined valuation of approximately $1.25 trillion. The all-stock deal positioned the new entity ahead of what is expected to be one of the largest initial public offerings in history later this year.

item.title: China's Yangtze fishing ban doubles fish biomass, study finds
item.description:
China's sweeping 10-year commercial fishing ban on the Yangtze River has halted seven decades of biodiversity decline, with fish biomass more than doubling and endangered species showing signs of recovery, according to new research published Thursday in the journal Science.

The study, which analyzed fish communities across 57 river reaches from 2018 to 2023, found that overall fish biomass increased by 209% and species richness rose by 13% following the implementation of the fishing ban in 2021. The recovery has been particularly pronounced among larger-bodied fish species occupying higher positions in the food web, including economically valuable species such as the black Amur bream and white Amur bream.

item.title: Nvidia shares stall as insiders sell $100M despite AI boom
item.description:
Nvidia shares have traded sideways in recent weeks, hovering near $185, even as major cloud providers announced record capital expenditure plans totaling nearly $700 billion for artificial intelligence infrastructure in 2026. The chipmaker is scheduled to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on February 25, with Wall Street expecting revenue of approximately $65 billion.

The disconnect between Nvidia's stock performance and the explosive growth in AI spending by its biggest customers has puzzled some investors. Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Microsoft collectively plan to spend between $635 billion and $665 billion this year, a roughly 70% increase from 2025, according to Yahoo Finance. The majority of this investment is directed toward AI chips, server infrastructure, and data center development.

item.title: Trump tells Zelenskyy to 'get moving' as Geneva talks set
item.description:
President Donald Trump issued an urgent public warning to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday, saying his counterpart must "get moving" on peace negotiations with Russia or risk missing a historic opportunity to end the nearly four-year conflict. The remarks came as both nations confirmed a third round of U.S.-brokered talks will take place in Geneva next week.

"Russia wants to make a deal, and Zelenskyy's gonna have to get moving—otherwise he's going to miss a great opportunity. He has to move," Trump told reporters while leaving the White House.

The Trump administration is pushing for a peace agreement by early summer, with Zelenskyy himself acknowledging last week that U.S. officials want the war concluded by June. In remarks to reporters in Kyiv, Zelenskyy said he understands the reasoning: American attention will soon shift to the November congressional midterm elections.

"The Americans are proposing the parties end the war by the beginning of this summer and will probably put pressure on the parties precisely according to this schedule," Zelenskyy said, adding candidly, "The elections are undoubtedly more significant for them. Let's not be naive".

item.title: Yangtze fishing ban halts 70 years of biodiversity decline
item.description: China's decade-long commercial fishing ban on the Yangtze River has halted 70 years of biodiversity decline and triggered early signs of ecological recovery, according to a comprehensive study published this week in the journal Science. Fish biomass has more than doubled, endangered species are rebounding, and the world's longest river system appears to be making a cautious comeback.

item.title: Macron urges Europe to become a geopolitical power at Munich
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron called on Europe to embrace its role as a geopolitical power and define its own security future in a keynote speech at the Munich Security Conference on Friday, delivering a pointed defense of the continent amid shifting transatlantic dynamics.

"This is the right time for audacity. This is the right time for a strong Europe," Macron declared, urging European leaders to shed self-doubt. "Europe has to learn to become a geopolitical power. It was not part of our DNA."

item.title: Fire erupts at Havana refinery as Cuba endures US oil blockade
item.description:
A fire erupted Friday at the Ñico López refinery in Havana Bay, dealing another blow to Cuba as the island nation struggles with an intensifying energy crisis caused by a U.S.-imposed oil blockade. Dense black smoke was seen rising from the facility, though authorities have not confirmed casualties or damage to oil storage tanks.

The blaze comes as Cuba has gone a full month without a major fuel delivery, according to data analytics firm Kpler cited by Bloomberg. Since the Trump administration's January 29 executive order threatening tariffs on any nation supplying oil to Cuba, the island's two primary suppliers—Venezuela and Mexico—have halted shipments, leaving the country's aging power infrastructure starved of the roughly 100,000 barrels of crude it needs daily.

item.title: Trump sends second carrier to Gulf as Iran fortifies nuclear site
item.description: Iran is reinforcing tunnel entrances at a major underground complex near its Natanz nuclear facility, according to new satellite imagery analyzed by the Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS), a U.S.-based think tank. The developments come as the Trump administration deploys additional military assets to the Middle East and nuclear negotiations between Washington and Tehran hang in the balance.

item.title: Zelensky says Ukraine won't hold referendum on 'bad' peace deal
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky offered a detailed account of his approach to peace negotiations with Russia in an exclusive interview with The Atlantic, published Thursday as he prepared to attend the Munich Security Conference. Speaking with journalist Simon Shuster, Zelensky emphasized Ukraine's willingness to engage constructively with U.S.-led proposals while setting firm conditions for any final agreement.

"The tactic we chose is for the Americans not to think that we want to continue the war," Zelensky told The Atlantic. "That's why we started supporting their proposals in any format that speeds things along."

item.title: Blue Origin reveals accelerated Moon plan as SpaceX pivots from Mars
item.description:
The race to return humans to the lunar surface has entered a new phase this week, with both SpaceX and Blue Origin unveiling aggressive strategies to beat China to the Moon, while Beijing continues to make steady progress toward its 2030 landing goal.

On February 9, Elon Musk announced a dramatic shift in SpaceX's priorities, revealing that the company has pivoted toward building a "self-growing city" on the Moon within the next decade. The announcement, made on his social media platform X, marks a stark reversal for the billionaire, who as recently as last year dismissed lunar missions as a "distraction" from his Mars ambitions. According to Reuters, Musk said traveling to Mars is only possible every 26 months, while launches to the Moon can occur every 10 days, allowing SpaceX to "iterate much faster."
